transcript: Operation Mincemeat might be the most lyrically dense musical that Broadway has seen since Hamilton. Making its much anticipated hop across the pond with its entire original West End cast, this is a sharp and high-speed musical comedy about the titular spy operation during World War II. It's not an obvious topic to make a musical about, but it totally works. The five ensemble members, some of whom are also writers of the piece, play dozens of characters, constantly and comedically switching between different costumes, voices, and physicalities. And impressively, this isn't confusing at all. I did feel there was some lyrical muddiness when everyone was singing together, especially during the most fast-paced numbers. I don't think giving the cast recording a listen beforehand would be a bad idea, but I also don't think I missed anything vital by being completely unfamiliar with it going in. Another observation was that it took me a little while to get into this, I think because the comedy is very British, and this doesn't align strongly with my sense of humor. But that's a matter of personal preference, and with just how plentiful the jokes are in this piece, everyone's bound to have some laughs. Overall, I was really impressed by this show. The book and lyrics are clever, the staging is super theatrical, and this cast is a well-oiled machine. The pacing is outstanding and it just flies — some of the transitions almost feel like magic tricks for how efficiently they're pulled off with just a cast of five. I was thoroughly entertained, and I think this is quite an achievement in writing and ensemble work. For these reasons, it's definitely a must-see this season. With that, another playbill for my collection.
